capabilities.capability: durable notes plus a bundle token you carry forward
capabilities.first_call: emem_memory_create (MCP) to write the note, then emem_memory_bundle to get one token to carry across the boundary
capabilities.use_instead: Use it as a handoff to your future self that anyone can also read. If the content must stay private, keep it in your own store, or self-host via /v1/guard/selfhost. Do not route secrets here on the strength of the word 'memory'.
when: I need state that survives context compaction
I need a checkpoint before my context window ends
I need to remember this after I am compacted
I need durable scratch memory for myself
capabilities.why_not: There is no private per-session checkpoint. /openapi.json routes no session, checkpoint or compaction endpoint, and a write lands in /memories/by_attester/<your pk8>/ which is world-readable. What works is the durable half: write the note, take a token, and dereference it after compaction. What does not work is privacy, and automatic capture, which you must do yourself before the window ends.

capabilities.first_call: POST /v1/attest for facts; MCP /mcp/full for notes
capabilities.use_instead: Attest facts over REST with POST /v1/attest, which is the signed write path that does have an HTTP door. For note-shaped memory, speak MCP at /mcp/full.
when: I need to write memory over plain HTTP, without an MCP client
I need a REST write path
my runtime does not speak MCP
can I curl a write
capabilities.why_not: Reads are fully available over REST, writes are not: emem_memory_create, insert, str_replace, rename and delete are MCP-only and have no REST twin. /openapi.json lists no write path, so a client that only speaks HTTP can read everything and write nothing.

capabilities.use_instead: Self-host with /v1/guard/selfhost, or keep private state in your own store and publish only the claims you want checkable. Namespace scoping stops another agent writing as you; it does not hide anything.
when: I need memory that is private to me
I need owner-scoped reads
nobody else should see this
I need per-tenant isolation
capabilities.why_not: There are no owner-scoped reads. Every note and fact written here is readable by anyone, by design: the protocol's value is that a third party can check a claim without trusting the writer, and that property is incompatible with a private read. Writes are namespace-scoped to your key, which controls who may WRITE where, not who may read.

capabilities.use_instead: Read freely: every read path is open and needs no key, no token and no account. Generate a keypair only when you want to write. Bearer tokens exist on the OAuth surface but gate nothing.
when: I need to participate without managing signing keys
I do not want to hold a private key
can the server sign for me
I need zero-setup writes
capabilities.why_not: Writing requires an ed25519 key you hold and a per-verb preimage you sign; there is no server-side signing route, and there should not be. A signature the responder could produce on your behalf would attest nothing about you, which would make every downstream verification meaningless.

provider.name: emem
provider.what: Shared, verifiable memory for AI agents. One place, one content-addressed address; one observation, one signed fact; one object, one citeable identity. Every read returns an ed25519 receipt any agent verifies offline, without trusting the responder.
